Kana usa ka dakong pasidaan! Pasabot niini nga tingali moabot ang tsunami, mao nga kinahanglan mobiya dayon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water flows through pipes because pressure pushes it!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that water moves due to pressure, but the competency is about exploring/demonstrating ways to make objects move by natural causes (wind, water) or by people. The card does not describe making an object move using water; it only explains water's own movement through pipes. No direct instructional support for the skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water flows through pipes because pressure pushes it!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out simple investigations to demonstrate that contact forces cause objects to move in the same direction as the direction that the force is applied
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires carrying out simple investigations to demonstrate that contact forces cause objects to move in the direction of the applied force. The card mentions pressure pushing water, which is a force, but it does not describe an investigation, contact force explicitly, or an object moving in the direction of the force. It is only a general statement about water pressure, not a demonstration of contact forces.

copy.en: Water flows through pipes because pressure pushes it! That's why when you open a faucet, the water comes right out.
copy.tl: Dumadaloy ang tubig sa mga tubo dahil sa presyon na nagtutulak! Kaya kapag binuksan ang gripo, lumalabas agad ang tubig.
copy.bis: Nagdagayday ang tubig sa mga tubo tungod sa presyon nga nagtukmod! Mao nga kon ablihan ang gripo, mogawas dayon ang tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It lays down sediment that grades from coarse grains at the bottom to fine grains at the top.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how a turbidite forms and the grading of sediment grains, but it does not involve exploring, collecting, or comparing different types of rocks by texture, color, or grain crystal size as required by G5-E-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A turbidite forms when an underwater landslide rushes across the ocean floor!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how fossils can be used for dating the age of rocks and sediments
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a sedimentary deposit and grain grading, but it does not explain how fossils are used for dating the age of rocks and sediments. Fossil dating is not addressed.

copy.en: A turbidite forms when an underwater landslide rushes across the ocean floor! It lays down sediment that grades from coarse grains at the bottom to fine grains at the top.
copy.tl: Ang turbidite ay nabubuo kapag ang isang underwater landslide ay dumaan sa ocean floor! Naglalagay ito ng sediment mula sa malalaking butil sa ibaba hanggang sa maliliit na butil sa itaas.
copy.bis: Ang turbidite naporma kon ang usa ka underwater landslide modagan sa ilawom sa dagat! Nagbutang kini og sediment nga nag-umpisa sa dagkong butil sa ubos hangtod sa gagmay nga butil sa ibabaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Turrones de casuy is a sweet made from cashew, the seed that grows on the outside of the fruit's soft part
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: A culinary cashew seed is food, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the seed that grows on the outside of the fruit's soft part
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: Seed position on a fruit is not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

copy.en:
What part of the fruit is cashew?

It's the seed! Turrones de casuy is a sweet made from cashew, the seed that grows on the outside of the fruit's soft part.
copy.tl:
Anong parte ng prutas ang kasuy?

Ito ang buto! Ang turones de casuy ay matamis na gawa sa kasuy, ang butong tumutubo sa labas ng malambot na bahagi ng prutas.
copy.bis:
Unsang bahin sa prutas ang kasuy?

Kini ang liso! Ang turones de casuy usa ka tam-is nga hinimo sa kasuy, ang liso nga motubo sa gawas sa humok nga bahin sa prutas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Turquoise is a gorgeous mineral that is famous for its beautiful blue-green color!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that turquoise is a mineral with a blue-green color. It does not involve exploring, observing, or collecting rocks, nor does it describe similarities/differences in features like texture, color, or grain crystal size. The content is merely a fact about a mineral, not instruction supporting the competency's investigative skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Turquoise is a gorgeous mineral that is famous for its beautiful blue-green color!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a physical property (color) of a solid material (turquoise mineral), but it does not describe the property in a way that teaches students to describe physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. It only names a color without elaboration or comparison, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Turquoise is a gorgeous mineral that is famous for its beautiful blue-green color!
copy.tl: Ang turquoise ay isang mineral na sikat sa kanyang magandang asul-berde na kulay!
copy.bis: Ang turquoise usa ka mineral nga sikat sa iyang nindot nga asul-berde nga kolor!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a turtle's shell is made from its own backbone and ribs, grown wide and joined together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: A shell made of backbone and ribs is not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a turtle's shell is made from its own backbone and ribs, grown wide and joined together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: A turtle shell fused from backbone and ribs is turtle skeleton anatomy, not the difference versus animals without backbones.

copy.en:
Is a turtle's shell like armor?

Not really — a turtle's shell is made from its own backbone and ribs, grown wide and joined together. It's part of the turtle's body, not something it wears.
copy.tl:
Sandata ba ang talukab ng pagong?

Hindi pala — gawa ang talukab ng pagong sa sarili nitong gulugod at tadyang na lumawak at nagdugtong. Bahagi ito ng katawan ng pagong, hindi kasuotan.
copy.bis:
Hinagiban ba ang talukab sa bao?

Dili diay — ang talukab sa bao hinimo gikan sa iyang kaugalingong gulugod ug gusok nga milapad ug naghiusa. Bahin kini sa lawas sa bao, dili sinul-ob.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's part of its skeleton, joined to its ribs and backbone, so it can't ever leave it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: A turtle shell joined to ribs and backbone is turtle skeleton anatomy, not the difference versus animals without backbones.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's part of its skeleton, joined to its ribs and backbone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: A turtle shell is not how the human skeletal system works.

copy.en:
Can a turtle leave its own shell?

Never! A turtle's shell isn't a house it wears — it's part of its skeleton, joined to its ribs and backbone, so it can't ever leave it.
copy.tl:
Puwede bang lumabas ang pagong sa talukab?

Hindi kailanman! Ang talukab ng pagong ay hindi bahay na suot lang — bahagi ito ng kalansay nito, nakakabit sa tadyang at gulugod, kaya di ito mahihiwalay.
copy.bis:
Makagawas ba ang bao sa iyang kabhang?

Dili gyud! Ang kabhang sa bao dili balay nga sul-obon lang — kabahin kini sa iyang kalabera, sumpay sa gusok ug bukog-likod, mao nga dili gyud kini makagawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Television broadcasting uses two carrier waves at once: AM carries the picture signals while FM carries the sound signals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in a guided investigation to identify the effect of different types of soil on the growth of plants
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses TV broadcasting and AM/FM carrier waves, which is unrelated to the competency about investigating the effect of different types of soil on plant growth. No soil or plant content is present.

copy.en: Television broadcasting uses two carrier waves at once: AM carries the picture signals while FM carries the sound signals, and both are sent by the same antenna.
copy.tl: Gumagamit ang television broadcasting ng dalawang carrier wave nang sabay: dinadala ng AM ang picture signals habang dinadala naman ng FM ang sound signals, at pareho itong ipinapadala ng iisang antenna.
copy.bis: Ang television broadcasting mogamit ug duha ka carrier wave sa usa ka higayon: gidala sa AM ang picture signals samtang gidala sa FM ang sound signals, ug pareho kini nga gipadala sa usa ra ka antenna.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sounds from directly in front and directly behind you reach both ears at the exact same time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sound localization and front-back confusion, not about how sound is made or transferred. It mentions sounds reaching the ears, but does not explore or describe sound production or transfer in the way the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sounds from directly in front and directly behind you reach both ears at the exact same time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses sound arriving at the ears, which implies sound traveling from a source to a receiver, but it does not identify that waves carry energy. The focus is on binaural timing and confusion, not on wave energy transfer.

copy.en:
Why do you sometimes mix up front and back sounds?

Sounds from directly in front and directly behind you reach both ears at the exact same time — that's why your brain sometimes gets confused until you turn your head!
copy.tl:
Bakit nalilito ka minsan kung saan galing ang tunog?

Ang tunog na nasa harap mo at nasa likod mo ay parehong layo sa iyong dalawang tainga, kaya sabay itong darating — dahil dito, nalilito ang utak mo hanggang lumingon ka!
copy.bis:
Nganong maglibog ka usahay diin gikan ang tingog?

Ang tingog nga anaa sa imong atubangan ug luyo managsama ang gilay-on sa duha nimo ka dalunggan, mao nga dungan kini moabot — mao nga maglibog ang imong utok hangtod molingi ka!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stereo headphones make sound seem to move from left to right
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains sound localization using stereo headphones, but it does not describe how sound is made or transferred, which is the focus of G3-F-4. It shares the broad topic of sound in everyday situations but gives no direct instructional support for sound production or transmission.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stereo headphones make sound seem to move from left to right
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a use of sound (headphones), but G4-F-10 requires observing and identifying sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy in school, home, and community settings. The card does not identify sound as a source of energy or its general uses; it only describes a specific auditory illusion, so it is related but not direct.

copy.en:
How do headphones trick your ears?

Stereo headphones make sound seem to move from left to right by playing it slightly louder or earlier on one side—copying the same clues your ears use in real life!
copy.tl:
Paano nilalaro ng headphones ang tainga mo?

Sa stereo headphones, parang gumagalaw ang tunog mula kaliwa papuntang kanan dahil mas malakas o mas maaga itong pinapatugtog sa isang tabi—ginagaya lang ang paraan ng tunay na pandinig!
copy.bis:
Giunsa paglimbong sa headphones ang dalunggan?

Sa stereo headphones, murag molihok ang tingog gikan sa wala paingon sa tuo kay mas kusog o mas sayo kini gipatugtog sa usa ka kilid—gisundog lang ang paagi sa tinuod nga pagdungog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound reaches the ear closer to it a tiny bit sooner and louder
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how the brain determines the direction of a sound using tiny differences in arrival time and loudness between the ears. This is about sound localization, not about how sound is made or transferred. The competency focuses on exploring and describing sound production and transfer in everyday situations (e.g., ringing bell, hearing noises). The card shares the topic of sound but does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: Sound reaches the ear closer to it a tiny bit sooner and louder — that tiny difference is enough for your brain to figure out the direction it came from!
copy.tl: Bahagyang mas maaga at mas malakas na umaabot ang tunog sa mas malapit na tainga — sapat na ang maliit na pagkakaibang ito para malaman ng utak ang direksyon nito!
copy.bis: Gamay nga mas sayo ug mas kusog nga moabot ang tingog sa mas duol nga dalunggan — igo na kining gamay nga kalainan aron mahibaloan sa utok ang direksyon niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Underwater, sound travels so fast it hits both your ears at almost the same time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sound transfer and hearing, but focuses on underwater speed and binaural localization, not on how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations like ringing bells or hearing noises. It does not directly teach the G3-F-4 skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Underwater, sound travels so fast it hits both your ears at almost the same time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sound traveling but does not use scientific wave terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity, nor does it describe wave properties. It is only tangentially related to sound waves.

copy.en:
Why is it hard to locate sound underwater?

Underwater, sound travels so fast it hits both your ears at almost the same time—so your brain loses the tiny clue it needs to tell which direction it came from!
copy.tl:
Bakit mahirap malaman kung saan galing ang tunog sa tubig?

Sa ilalim ng tubig, napakabilis kumalat ng tunog kaya halos sabay itong umaabot sa dalawang tainga mo—kaya nawawala sa utak mo ang maliit na sangguni para malaman kung saan galing!
copy.bis:
Nganong lisod mahibal-an kung asa gikan ang tingog sa ilawom sa tubig?

Sa ilawom sa tubig, paspas kaayo mokatag ang tingog nga halos dungan kining moabot sa duha nimo ka dalunggan—mao nga mawala sa utok ang gamayng timailhan para mahibal-an kung asa gikan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: like charges repel each other and opposite charges attract
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the fundamental rule of electric charge interaction, which is necessary background for investigating static electricity, but it does not involve the required investigation using common materials (comb, rods, balloons) nor describe effects of static electricity in those contexts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How do electric charges interact?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses electric forces between charges, but G7-F-1 is about identifying that forces act between objects and can be measured, typically referring to mechanical forces and measurement. The card does not address measurement or the general concept of forces between objects beyond charge interaction.

copy.en:
How do electric charges interact?

There are two kinds of electric charge, positive and negative; like charges repel each other and opposite charges attract!
copy.tl:
Paano nagtutugon ang mga elektrikal na karga?

May dalawang uri: positibo at negatibo. Ang magkaparehong karga ay nagtataboy, at ang magkasalungat ay umaakit!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa duha ka electric charge?

Adunay positibo ug negatibo. Ang parehas nga charge magsalikway, ug ang magkalahi magdani!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The first letter is always capital, and the second letter is always lowercase, like He for helium!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the names and symbols of the first 20 or several common elements of the periodic table
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the capitalization rule for writing two-letter element symbols and gives one example (He). It does not identify the names and symbols of the first 20 or several common elements, which is the core action of G8-M-6. The rule is useful background for writing symbols but does not directly support identifying element names and symbols.

copy.en:
How do we write two-letter element symbols correctly?

The first letter is always capital, and the second letter is always lowercase, like He for helium!
copy.tl:
Paano natin isinusulat nang tama ang mga dalawang-letrang simbolo ng elemento?

Ang unang titik ay laging malaki, at ang pangalawa ay laging maliit, gaya ng He para sa helium!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagsulat sa tarong sa duha ka letra nga simbolo sa elemento?

Ang unang letra kanunay dako, ug ang ikaduha kanunay gamay, sama sa He para sa helium!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines sits where tectonic plates push together! That's why volcanoes and earthquakes keep happening in the same broad belts.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a general cause of volcanic and earthquake belts (plate convergence) but does not address patterns of volcanic eruptions over the last 100 years, predictability, or discussion with family/community as required by the competency.

copy.en: The Philippines sits where tectonic plates push together! That's why volcanoes and earthquakes keep happening in the same broad belts.
copy.tl: Nasa Pilipinas ang lugar kung saan nagdidikit ang mga tectonic plates! Kaya patuloy na may bulkan at lindol sa malawak na belts.
copy.bis: Naa sa Pilipinas ang dapit diin nagtapok ang mga tectonic plates! Mao nga kanunay nga adunay bulkan ug linog sa halapad nga belts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Since it is warm all year, we wear light clothes! During the wet season, we just use umbrellas or raincoats to stay dry.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'wet season' and warm weather but does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities appropriate for each season. It only gives a clothing example, which is not the core skill of describing seasons and suggesting activities.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During the wet season, we just use umbrellas or raincoats to stay dry.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in the weather can affect daily activities and explain how some types of weather can be dangerous for people
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on how weather (wet season) affects daily clothing choices, but it does not describe how changes in weather affect daily activities broadly, nor does it explain dangerous weather types. The content is only a minor example, not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
What clothes do we wear in the Philippines?

Since it is warm all year, we wear light clothes! During the wet season, we just use umbrellas or raincoats to stay dry.
copy.tl:
Anong damit ang suot natin sa Pilipinas?

Dahil mainit buong taon, magaan na damit ang suot natin! Tuwing tag-ulan, payong o kapote na lang ang gamit natin para hindi mabasa.
copy.bis:
Unong sinina ang atong suot sa Pilipinas?

Tungod kay init tibuok tuig, magaan nga sinina ang atong suot! Panahon sa ting-ulan, payong o kapote na lang ang gamit nato para dili mabasa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tiny particles scatter the light to show its path
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Tyndall effect (light scattering by particles) but does not mention mixtures, solutions, suspensions, or uniform/non-uniform classification. It provides no direct instructional support for describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a flashlight beam passes through smoke or milky water, tiny particles scatter the light to show its path
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves light behavior (scattering) and a light source, but it does not guide students to explore sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, or its uses in everyday situations. It only states a single phenomenon without any guided activity or broader exploration.

copy.en: When a flashlight beam passes through smoke or milky water, tiny particles scatter the light to show its path. This is the Tyndall effect!
copy.tl: Kapag dumaan ang flashlight sa usok o gatas na tubig, ikinakalat ng maliliit na particle ang liwanag para makita ang daan. Ito ang Tyndall effect!
copy.bis: Kon moagi ang flashlight sa aso o gatas nga tubig, gikatag sa gagmayng partikulo ang kahayag aron makita ang agianan. Kini ang Tyndall effect!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a true solution, light passes straight through without scattering, so there is no Tyndall effect!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a property of true solutions (no Tyndall effect) but does not describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. It does not directly support the competency's focus on examples of mixture types.

copy.en:
Does a true solution show the Tyndall effect?

In a true solution, light passes straight through without scattering, so there is no Tyndall effect!
copy.tl:
Nagpapakita ba ng Tyndall effect ang isang tunay na solusyon?

Sa tunay na solusyon, ang liwanag ay dumadaan nang hindi ikinakalat kaya walang Tyndall effect!
copy.bis:
Nagpakita ba ang tinuod nga solusyon sa Tyndall effect?

Sa tinuod nga solusyon, moagi ang kahayag nga dili ikatag mao nga walay Tyndall effect!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pure type AB parents carry no O gene, so they can never pass type O blood to their child.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses ABO blood type inheritance, which involves multiple alleles and codominance, not a simple dominant/recessive characteristic. It also does not represent inheritance through generations of a family as the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pure type AB parents carry no O gene, so they can never pass type O blood to their child.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict simple ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes in crosses involving dominant/recessive gene pairs
assignedReviews.reason: The card makes a qualitative claim about one cross but does not predict simple ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes for dominant/recessive gene pairs. ABO blood type is not a simple dominant/recessive trait, and no ratio or Punnett-square style prediction is provided.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pure type AB parents carry no O gene, so they can never pass type O blood to their child.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions genes being passed but does not explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in trait transmission. It only states a blood-type inheritance fact without explaining the underlying genetic mechanism.

copy.en:
Can two type AB parents have a type O child?

No! Pure type AB parents carry no O gene, so they can never pass type O blood to their child.
copy.tl:
Puwede bang magkaanak ng Type O ang dalawang magulang na AB?

Hindi puwede! Walang O gene ang puro Type AB na magulang, kaya hindi nila maipapasa ang Type O sa anak.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang mabatonan ug Type O nga anak ang duha ka ginikanang AB?

Dili gyud mahimo! Ang puro Type AB nga ginikanan walay O gene, mao nga dili sila makapasa og Type O sa anak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has only ONE possible genotype, IAIB!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict simple ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes in crosses involving dominant/recessive gene pairs
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the AB blood type genotype but does not involve crosses, ratios, or dominant/recessive gene pairs. Blood type AB is an example of codominance, not simple dominant/recessive inheritance, so it does not directly support predicting offspring ratios.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has only ONE possible genotype, IAIB!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not represent patterns of inheritance through generations of a family. It only notes that AB has a single genotype, which is a genetics fact but not a demonstration of inheritance patterns for a simple dominant/recessive characteristic.

copy.en:
Why is blood type AB special in genetics?

It has only ONE possible genotype, IAIB! There's no 'pure' version like AA or BB — AB always needs an A gene and a B gene together.
copy.tl:
Bakit kakaiba ang blood type AB sa genetics?

Iisa lang ang posibleng genotype nito, ang IAIB! Wala itong 'puro' na bersyon gaya ng AA o BB — laging kailangan ng A gene AT B gene nang sabay para maging AB.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga espesyal ang blood type AB sa genetics?

Usa ra ang posible nga genotype niini, ang IAIB! Walay 'puro' nga bersyon sama sa AA o BB — kanunayng gikinahanglan ang A gene UG B gene nga dungan aron mahimong AB.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People with Type O blood have no A or B antigen at all on their red blood cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Type O antigens are typing, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: no A or B antigen at all on their red blood cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: Antigens on red cells are not microscope techniques for cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts.

copy.en: People with Type O blood have no A or B antigen at all on their red blood cells.
copy.tl: Ang taong may dugong Type O ay walang A o B antigen sa kanilang mga pulang selula ng dugo.
copy.bis: Ang tawo nga may dugo nga Type O walay A o B antigen sa ilang mga pula nga selula sa dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: about 20 tropical cyclones enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a map and a record of tracking data to trace the path of typhoons that enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR)
